newsitem.title: POLAND: Boryszew registered shares clear to trade.
newsitem.headline: Boryszew registered shares clear to trade.

text.p: The Polish Securities Commission (KPW) cleared 644,250 registered, preferred shares of Polish chemical firm Boryszew SA for public trade, KPW head Jacek Socha told a news conference on Thursday.

Boryszew President Grzegorz Kalisiak told Reuters after the conference that in the next few months about 30 percent of holders of the registered shares, which have twice the voting power of a common share, would likely convert their shares.
In December Boryszew shareholders approved management's proposal to convert 644,250 registered shares into common shares for public trade.
"These are shares of the firm's founders, and we wanted all the firm's shares to have the same rights so that they could all trade on the bourse," Kalisiak told the news conference.
Currently Boryszew has 2,244,250 shares outstanding, of which are the 644,250 registered and privileged ones.

Kalisiak also said the firm aimed for pvc siding to account for 10 percent of its sales in the next two to three years. Last month the firm said it expected sales to rise to 120.7 million zlotys this year from 99.9 million in 1996.
